content.name: Sofya Zamaraeva
content.description:
I am an ofsted registered childminder.

I offer funded entitlement places to 9 months, 2, 3 and 4 years old children.

I was rated with a "good" grade on my last inspection. 

Some of my qualifications include childcare and first aid.

I love working with children and keeping busy with lots of fun activities and learning for the children.

I am a hard-working person, as well as someone you can trust.

taxonomies.name: 9 month to 2 year olds funded providers

local_offer.description: I am providing a safe, friendly, warm environment and offer support and activities according to each individual need.

survey_answers.question: What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families?
survey_answers.answer: I record children’s development and progress with starting points, regular assessments, next steps, 2-year checks and consultations with parents.

survey_answers.question: What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?
survey_answers.answer: I do not have any special needs qualifications, but I would be willing to do more training to help any child within my setting.

survey_answers.question: How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?
survey_answers.answer: I will discuss any SEND issues with parents and make plans together for the best welfare of their child.

survey_answers.answer: I have restricted wheelchair access  ground floor toilet facilities.

content.name: Big Top Nursery Waddesdon
content.description: Full day care, open 51 weeks per year.

organisation.name: Big Top Nurseries (Part of the Kindred Family)

taxonomies.name: 9 month to 2 year olds funded providers

local_offer.description: Big Top Nursery has recently become part of the Kindred Family, we cater for up to 60 children per session.  We welcome all children and families and will make all reasonable adjustments to meet their needs.   We aim to build positive relationships with the children and their families.  We want parents to be fully involved with the nursery and to share their children’s successes, achievements, concerns and hopes for the future.  We have high aspirations for all children and aim to work together with parents to support each child to develop and learn in their own way and at their own pace.

survey_answers.question: What outcomes does your setting, service or activity aim to achieve for children and young people with SEND and their families?
survey_answers.answer:
Our SENCO Sophie attends the termly Local Authority SENCO Liaison Groups.
The setting has access to advice from The Early Years SEND, Access and Inclusion Team, through telephone consultations or with parental agreement, child specific advice from an Early Years SEND Advisor.
A range of online resources (Communication Carousel, IDP, OT and SALT websites)
We are happy for professionals involved with the child to visit and welcome this opportunity to develop our knowledge.  We have close links with the local Children’s Centre and Health Visitors’ team.
We are happy to attend Multi-Professional Meetings

survey_answers.question: What recent SEND-specific training has been completed by your staff and/or volunteers?
survey_answers.answer: Sophie has many years experience of working with children within the setting who have additional needs. Sophie has attended Sendco training, attends termly meetings and has recently signed up to complete a Level 3 Sendco qualification.

survey_answers.question: How do you involve parents and how can I get involved?
survey_answers.answer: Parents have access to our online record system and we encourage them to add their own observations, photos and events from home. Parents can request a meeting with their child’s Key Person at any time and an appointment will be made as soon as possible.  We will meet regularly with parents to update on your child’s progress and discuss their likes, dislikes, achievements and any concerns you may have.

survey_answers.question: How will you share information with me about my child’s progress? What is additional for children with SEND?
survey_answers.answer: The above opportunities are available for all parents/carers but in addition to this we welcome more frequent opportunities to meet with parents of children with SEND; how often will be discussed and agreed with the parents.  We also offer updates through home/school books, email or phone calls if this is more convenient.  We will regularly monitor the short term outcomes for children with SEND and would invite parents to be part of this review and the planning session for new outcomes.  If other professionals (Speech and Language Therapist, Occupational Therapist (OT)) are visiting we would aim to give parents the opportunity to meet with them on their visits too.

survey_answers.question: How accessible is the environment (indoors and outdoors)?
survey_answers.answer:
Our nursery is set over 2 floors.  Our baby and toddlers are on the lower floor, and our 2 to 4 year olds are on the 1st floor.  This is accessible via 2 flights of stairs.  This may cause issues for access.  However, we do have an entrance to our garden area that will then allow access to the upper floor, with 1 flight of stairs rather than 2.  Dependant on the child's needs, we may be able to support them within the baby/toddler room should it be appropriate to do so.
Our outside space is all on one level and consists of wet pour and fake grass.

survey_answers.question: How can children and young people with SEND and their families start to use your service or activity?
survey_answers.answer:
We understand that each child’s transition needs are individual and aim to work with parents by offering a range of options, including home visits, frequent settling sessions, shortened sessions and transition booklets.  We will be happy to discuss with you what you think would work best for your child and be flexible to meet their needs.
We have close relationships with the local schools and invite them to visit all children when they are transferring.

survey_answers.question: What future plans do you have for developing your SEND provision?
survey_answers.answer: We are currently auditing the SEND skills and knowledge of practitioners and will plan our training accordingly.
